sources.author: Swyx (Shawn Wang)
sources.headline: Head of Developer Experience @ Smol AI | AI Engineer
sources.post_summary: Posted a breakdown of the 'context window arms race' — why Claude 4's 1M token window changes agent architecture fundamentally. Argues most multi-agent setups are just workarounds for small context, and now that's a solved problem. Thread went viral among AI engineers debating whether long-context kills RAG.

sources.author: Lilian Weng
sources.headline: VP of Research @ OpenAI
sources.post_summary: Shared a quiet observation: the orgs shipping production AI agents fastest right now aren't the ones with the best models — they're the ones who solved memory and state persistence first. Referenced internal benchmarks showing agent reliability doubles when you separate working memory from long-term retrieval. No deck, no slides — just the insight.

sources.author: Theo Browne
sources.headline: CEO @ t3.gg | Builder of things on the internet
sources.post_summary: Hot take post: 'Claude Code just made senior engineers 10x more valuable, not replaceable.' Made the case that the ceiling on what one developer can ship in a week has completely broken — but only for people who already understand the stack. Junior devs copy-pasting AI output are shipping bugs at 10x speed. Sparked 400+ comment debate.

sources.author: Eno Reyes
sources.headline: Infrastructure Engineer @ Modal | Previously AWS
sources.post_summary: Posted a cost teardown of running 100 concurrent AI agents for a month — GPU hours, API tokens, egress, orchestration overhead broken down line by line. The surprise finding: inference cost is now the smallest line item. Orchestration infra and retry logic are eating the budget. Practical takeaways for teams building at scale.

sources.author: Kyle Coleman
sources.headline: CMO at Clari | Revenue Intelligence | GTM Strategy
sources.post_summary: Most outbound sequences are built backwards. You pick a tool, then craft messaging around its constraints. The best GTM teams I've seen flip this: write the message first, then pick the channel and cadence that serves it. AI can generate 1,000 personalized emails — but if the core message is wrong, you've just automated failure at scale.

sources.author: Jen Allen-Knuth
sources.headline: Community Growth at Lavender | Former Chief Evangelist | Sales Nerd
sources.post_summary: SDRs aren't dying — the spray-and-pray SDR is dying. What's replacing it is a new role: GTM engineer. Part ops, part builder, part analyst. They write Clay tables before breakfast and A/B test subject lines before lunch. The companies hiring for this hybrid role are running circles around teams with 10x the headcount.

sources.author: Tito Bohrt
sources.headline: CEO at AltiSales | Outbound Sales Expert | Revenue Leader
sources.post_summary: We ran the same outbound campaign with two lists: one bought from ZoomInfo, one built from first-party signals (job changes + tech installs + LinkedIn engagement). Reply rate on the signal-based list was 4.1% vs 0.6% on the ZoomInfo pull. Same sequence, same reps, same offer. The data is the moat now — not the copy.

sources.author: Gaetano DiNardi
sources.headline: Demand Gen Advisor | Former VP Marketing at Nextiva & Aura
sources.post_summary: Content strategy in 2026: stop publishing for Google, start publishing for AI. Your buyers are asking Claude and ChatGPT what tools to use before they ever touch a search bar. If your brand isn't in the training data or showing up in AI answers, you're invisible to a growing slice of your pipeline. This is the new SEO — and most teams aren't playing it yet.

sources.author: Priya Nair
sources.headline: Solo founder | Built and sold my first SaaS in 18 months | Now building #2
sources.post_summary: Priya shares a raw breakdown of her MRR journey from $0 to $12k — including the month she almost quit. She posts a simple chart, no fancy design, and ends with 'the unglamorous middle is where most people quit.' The vulnerability and specificity of the revenue numbers drove massive reshares.

sources.author: Marcus Delgado
sources.headline: Ex-nurse → self-taught developer | Shipping apps that matter | Career pivoter
sources.post_summary: Marcus documents week 14 of his coding journey after leaving a 9-year nursing career. He just shipped his first paying customer — a scheduling tool for home health aides. The post is a single photo of his laptop screen at 11pm with one line: 'First $49. It's real now.' Comments flooded with people mid-pivot saying 'this is exactly what I needed to see.'

sources.author: Tom Brewster
sources.headline: Vibe coder | Shipped 6 products with Claude Code | No CS degree, no problem
sources.post_summary: Tom shares a thread-style post cataloging the 6 micro-SaaS products he shipped in 90 days using AI coding tools — total cost under $200, total revenue $3.1k. He breaks down which ones flopped and why, without hiding failures. The honesty about what didn't work is what made it go viral in dev circles.

sources.author: Daniela Fontaine
sources.headline: PM turned founder | Building B2B tools for ops teams | 2 kids, 1 startup
sources.post_summary: Daniela posts a candid account of closing her first $500/mo B2B contract — signed on a Thursday afternoon between school pickup and dinner. She talks about the specific cold outreach message that worked (and pastes it verbatim), which sent the post into reshare territory. Ends with: 'No playbook. Just iterations.'
